Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
17 October 2026 .
Brent $ 109.86 + 3.72 % · Transits 2 (2026-10-11) · AI-assisted
01 Reuters reports Iran's Guards say two tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz, with one tanker catching fire, per Deccan Chronicle.

02 A projectile struck tanker MT ST 3 in the strait, with 15 Indian crew reported safe, per moneycontrol.com.

03 Brent settled at $109.86, up 3.72% in the last session before the close; WTI stood at $101.41.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed to commercial traffic, with mine strikes now the dominant hazard for vessels attempting transit. Reuters reports Iran's Guards say two tankers hit mines in the strait; Deccan Chronicle separately reports one tanker caught fire after striking a mine, attributing the claim to Iran's Guards. Iranian state media, including IRNA, report a second supertanker exploded after hitting a naval mine, a claim carried by WANA News Agency, Rudaw, Hindustan Times, and Al Arabiya English, though it originates with Iranian state media and no maritime authority has confirmed it. Separately, moneycontrol.com reports 15 Indian crew members are safe after the tanker MT ST 3 was struck by a projectile in the strait; Al Arabiya English reports a tanker exploded after hitting a mine, and Middle East Eye reports the IRGC has declared the strait closed. IMF PortWatch recorded 2 transits on October 11, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. Brent settled at $109.86, up 3.72% in the last session before the close; WTI stood at $101.41. The feed indexed 79 headlines in the past 24 hours. As of 15:22 UTC, 173 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the high band, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
